title: Happy Birthday
label: Meher Baba Association Ltd
description: This ultra-rare spiritual oddity finds the Who's main wrecker teaming up with Faces' most underrated rambler for a deeply bent tribute to their shared guru, resulting in something that sounds like a drunken philosophy seminar backed by the most restrained rhythm section this side of a meditation retreat. Townshend's earnest God-bothering gets filtered through Lane's cockney folk wisdom, creating a disarmingly intimate document that makes their respective bands' stadium bombast seem positively crass by comparison. Limited pressing means you'll probably never hear this unless you know someone who bought it at a Meher Baba center in '77, which is exactly how cosmic accidents like this should circulate.

title: The Blue Yusef Lateef
label: Atlantic, Atlantic
description: Yusef's Atlantic debut finds the Detroit multi-instrumentalist threading the needle between hard bop orthodoxy and the free-jazz maelstrom that was already consuming lesser talents like so much bad acid. Armed with his usual arsenal of exotic Eastern instruments and a rhythm section that swings harder than a wrecking ball through a condemned jazz club, Lateef delivers modal workouts that would make even Rahsaan Roland Kirk weep with envy. This is the sound of a master craftsman who understood that you don't need to abandon melody to embrace chaos – a lesson lost on about 90% of the longhairs who thought "freedom" meant forgetting how to actually play their goddamn instruments.
